copy.blurb:
The model fancies Côte d'Ivoire more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against Germany. +7.7pp is a substantive gap; that's what fires this as a Pick on the away side.

Elo numbers going in: Germany 1900, Côte d'Ivoire 1720. That's a 180-point lead for Germany — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Germany to win at 60%, the draw at 19%, and Côte d'Ivoire to win at 21%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Kalshi: Germany to win at 62%, the draw at 19%, and Côte d'Ivoire to win at 14%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Côte d'Ivoire side — 14% on the market, 21% on the engine, a +7.7pp gap.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Côte d'Ivoire the lower bound is 17%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +3.5pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The claim is narrow: on this fixture, on this side, the price is below what the underlying read supports. We don't argue the market is broadly wrong — across the priced field the model and the line agree more often than they disagree. We surface the ones where they don't.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 29 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read. Two outlets covered the build-up this week — BBC Sport (football): "Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer comes out of international retirement to be named in Germany's squad for the 2026 World Cup, with…"; The Guardian (football): "Yes I plan with [Neuer as No 1]"
drivers: Pre-match Elo gives Côte d'Ivoire a stronger prior than the Kalshi line implies.
The +7.7pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
This is a selection call on the Côte d'Ivoire side, not a blanket read on the market.
Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.

editorial_citations.quote: Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer comes out of international retirement to be named in Germany's squad for the 2026 World Cup, with manager Julian Nagelsmann saying the 40-year-old will be his team's number one for the tournament.
Yes I plan with [Neuer as No 1]
The main task was to nominate the best three keepers. So we decided that these three are part of that. We contacted Manuel and asked him if he wanted to play for the national team again.

copy.summary: The away side reads stronger to the model than to the market. Our Elo prior puts Côte d'Ivoire at 21%; Kalshi prices that side at 14%. The +7.7pp gap calls a Pick.
